content: Inhaled insulin is a viable option for insulin administration and has been shown in studies to exhibit a pharmacodynamic profile similar to that of rapid-acting insulin aspart. However, it is contraindicated in individuals with pre-existing lung diseases or those who smoke, due to potential respiratory complications. Furthermore, all patients who are prescribed inhaled insulin must undergo forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) testing to confirm that it is safe for them to use this method of insulin delivery.
